title: CLR/136/2019 of UMESH CHANDRA SHARMA Vs HEMCHANDRA BALUTIYA

paras.text:
CLR No.136 of 2019
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
 Mr. Piyush Garg, Advocate for the revisionist.
Mr. Sanpreet Singh Ajmani, Advocate for the
respondent.
This is a regular revision under Section 25 of the
Provincial Small Cause Courts Act whereby the
defendant has challenged the judgment and decree
dated 21.09.2019 as rendered in SCC Suit No.17 of
2010, Hem Chandra Balutiya vs. Umesh Chandra
Sharma and another. As a consequence to the judgment
impugned, the SCC Suit has been decreed and the
revisionist has been directed to pay the decreetal
amount with regard to the arrears of rent and damages
as it has been mentioned in the judgment dated
21.09.2019. The respondent landlord is represented
through his counsel.
It is an admitted case of the counsel for the parties
that during the pendency of proceedings, the revisionist
has made certain deposit before the court below that is
being directed to be remitted to the respondent landlord.
The counsel for the parties have submitted that
owing to the financial condition of the revisionist, the
landlord has expressed his compassion by waiving of
his right to received the decreetal amount thus
determined subject to the condition that the revisionist
gives an undertaking within two weeks from today
before the trial court that he would be vacating the
premises and handing over peaceful vacant possession
within three months thereafter i.e. latest by 28.02.2020.
Subject to the aforesaid undertaking the judgment
impugned would not be given effect to and as a
consequence thereto, the revision in view of the above
terms of settlement stands dismissed.
However, it is made clear that the undertaking as
directed above is not given within the time specified or
the vacant possession is not handed over to the landlord
respondent within the time given thereon. It will be
open for the respondent landlord to get the decree
executed in accordance with law.
 (Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.) 21.11.2019
